newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: APEC should have currency rate voice - Anwar.
newsitem.headline: APEC should have currency rate voice - Anwar.

text.p: The views of groups like APEC on international exchange rates need to be heard, Malaysian Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Sunday.
He also told Reuters Financial Television that he was comfortable with the recent exchange rate strength of the ringgit.

A communique to be released on Sunday by the APEC finance ministers holding their annual meeting here, is expected to say that major misalignments in currency rates have been corrected. The statement is also expected to refer to the economic risks of rates not based on fundamentals.
Anwar said APEC's currency comments are partly in response to the Group of Seven (G7).
He said: "We think that any intervention or various expressions on the issue should take into consideration all the international community and not be confined to the established group."

Asked if APEC was getting aggressive on rates, he said: "I don't think it's a question of aggressiveness. It is a question of gaining confidence and realising the need to have an effective mechanism of our own and not to be susceptible to unpredictable developments."
On recent strength of the ringgit, Anwar said: "I'm comfortable. I trust and have confidence in the central bank to manage it."
He said he was not concerned about an unhealthy inflow of speculative funds because speculators know Malaysia will act when necessary to prevent such a trend.
